correctness.rationale: The white-profile proof is exhaustive: with at least three whites any first force leaves at least two whites in one part and then stalls; with two whites, forcing succeeds exactly for a cross-part pair not drawn from two singleton parts. This characterizes all minimum sets, and every larger zero forcing set contains one in the noncomplete case. Direct simulation over 128 multipartite types and 64,916 subsets through order ten confirms the classification, counts, and irrelevant vertices.

value.rationale: Well-forcedness is a named structural property introduced to distinguish graphs where inclusion-minimal forcing solutions never have avoidable excess. Complete multipartite graphs form a canonical dense family with arbitrary twin classes. The theorem resolves the property on this family, classifies every minimal solution, and answers the accompanying irrelevant-vertex question with a sharp star exception.
